title: Johnny Dunn and Mamie Smith at the Lyric and Midnight Rambles
summary: Punch describes the Lyric's changing weekly shows and the late Midnight Rambles for white patrons.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did anybody use a plunger down here? Well, there was until after that.

Until after Johnny Dunn? Johnny Dunn, after that, when he came out of that plunger. Everybody started getting up. What was he doing here? Well, he come down with Mammy Smith. They played the Lyric Theater. They played the Lyric Theater and it was there a whole week. Who all would come to the Lyric? Oh, Lord, man. That lyric just would be crowded every day of the week. Every day of the week, upstairs and downstairs. You see, the first three days of the show come in, they play Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. Well, the next three days they change the show all the way around. That'd make the people come back again. See, the new show, see, be the same people but the new show, the new show they do. They wouldn't do the same show they did Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. They'd do another show and that'd make the third of the people just part of it again. And Saturday and Friday and Midnight Rambles. They did it. What were those Midnight Rambles? Oh, well, it was a little nasty, you know, different. Different. Hmm. How late would that start? That would start at 11 and end up around 2.

What night did they let the white people in? Us on Ramble Nights. On Ramble Nights. What about that Weeping Willow Blues? How did you play that? You told me you played that with Bessie once or something. Did you play that with Bessie? Weeping Willow?
